title: Word formation and lexical families
prior_teaching_boundary: Read every active ch01–ch13 contract and actual cumulative registers. Only individually recorded forms, senses and frames establish prerequisites; no archived teaching is inherited.
productive_outcomes: Analyse selected attested compounds through their components, final head and separately added inflection, retaining the checked whole-word meaning.
Distinguish derivation from inflection in the assigned prefix, noun-suffix, adjective and adverb families; do not infer unrestricted lexical coinage.
Use all productive cells of the complete eighteen selected noun systems and twenty separately defined verbal systems, with their diagnostic stems and exceptions together.

Use each newly assigned ordinary lexical sense and frame, including return, belief, leaving peace, giving, falling upon, praying reflexively, showing, licking, raising, mercy, receiving and providing friends.
Distinguish the new lexical noun gōd goods from the previously taught adjective rihtwīs used substantivally; preserve the actual governed case and agreement.
Complete all twenty-one unchanged Cook VIII.26–27 prompts and the original graded practice, distinguishing grammatical alternatives from explicitly stated vocabulary, number and final-verb controls.
recognition_outcomes: Interpret the complete 159-word source argument through its stated local supports, tracking the tall tree, cliffs, mountains and human conclusion.
Identify the passage’s paired words, repeated height vocabulary and repeated conclusions without mechanically treating near-synonyms as separate events.
Recognize the explicit reference-only noun number cells and supplied citation/source forms without inferring additional productive senses or full unassigned systems.
Distinguish an original source prompt or text from declared formatting normalization, supplied help and new teaching material.
bounded_scope: No unrestricted compound or derivative coinage.
No new full paradigms from source-only or citation forms.
Material/abstract number references retain their cell and sense limits.
Unit15 general negation/quantity remains outside this unit.
The second Dangers paragraph is unassigned.

explicit_scope_metrics.formation_scope: Analysis of attested and supplied families; no arbitrary formation or dictionary-free semantic prediction.
explicit_scope_metrics.reference_number_scope: All eight noun cases/numbers are displayed; material/abstract plurals and the singular of gōd goods retain the audit’s recognition/reference limits.
explicit_scope_metrics.nonfinite_scope: The four new participle pairs teach bases; only the past bases enter the separately taught passive use. No new full attributive participle declensions are inferred.
explicit_scope_metrics.supplied_scope: Exact negative and indefinite expressions, rare finite forms, participial phrases, proper-name forms and difficult source constructions remain visibly supported.
explicit_scope_metrics.later_scope: General negation, quantity and further discourse comparison remain Unit15; the following luxury/death paragraph is unassigned.

audited_inflection_rules.description: Complete strong masculine singular/plural: uninflected nominative/accusative singular; -es, -e; plural -as, -a, -um, -as.
Complete strong heavy-stem neuter singular/plural: nominative/accusative singular and plural without ending; -es, -e; plural genitive -a and dative -um. Compounds follow the final nominal component.

Long/heavy feminine model ār: nominative singular uninflected; genitive/dative/accusative -e; plural nominative/accusative/genitive -a, dative -um. The alternate genitive plural -ena is not the selected route.
Feminine -nes doubles s before inflectional endings; the full singular/plural follows the long feminine model.
Weak masculine: nominative singular -a; other singular and nominative/accusative plural -an; genitive plural -ena; dative plural -um.

Weak neuter ēage has nominative/accusative singular ēage; genitive/dative singular ēagan; nominative/accusative plural ēagan; genitive plural ēagena (also ēagna); dative plural ēagum. Cook §53.2 explicitly gives neuter equality of nominative and accusative.

Wuldor uses the syncopated stem wuldr- before endings, by §§43.4 and 47.6. The selected reference nominative/accusative plural wuldru applies the admitted disyllabic neuter -u route (§47.1); it is a rule-derived reference cell, not a claim of corpus attestation or a new lexical plural meaning.

audited_inflection_rules.statement: WeakI selected present -e,-st,-ð,-að; dental past -de/-dest/-de/-don. gewęnd- and sęnd- simplify -ndd- to -nd- in the preterite; present d devoices before -st/-ð. gelīefan retains long īe; selected past gelīefde. ætīewan retains w in this selected long-stem system. gemētan contracts the participle dental to gemētt. ge- already belongs to geglęngan/gewęndan/gemētan; these selected forms do not add a second ge-.

WeakII selected present -ie,-ast,-að,-iað; past -ode,-odest,-ode,-odon; imperative singular -a, plural -iað. liccian retains both c letters throughout the selected stem; tilian has one l and gemiltsian has ts. Variant -ige/-ade patterns are unassigned.

StrongV selected four-stem systems: gief/geaf/gēaf/gief, bidd/bæd/bǣd/bed. Prefixes remain part of the attested lexeme: forgiefan/gebiddan. Present gebitst/gebitt simplify the geminate+dental; second singular preterite uses the plural stem, forgēafe/gebǣde.

āhrēosan follows the s-stem strongII pattern: āhrēos/āhrēas/āhrur/āhror; present second/third singular āhrīest, with long īe selected by the Cook umlaut rule. The past plural/second-singular r is lexical grammatical alternation, not an arbitrary ending substitution.

āhębban follows the checked hębban pattern, preserving ā-: āhębbe/āhęfst/āhęfð/āhębbað, preterite āhōf/āhōfe/āhōfon; participle diagnostic āhafen. Double b in the first singular/plural becomes f before the second/third singular ending.

onfōn follows the contracted fōn pattern: onfō/onfēhst/onfēhð/onfōð; preterite onfēng/onfēnge/onfēngon; participle diagnostic onfangen. Receive retains its separately taught dative object, unlike earlier catch+accusative fōn.

Subjunctive singular uses one form for all persons and plural one -n form for all persons. Strong present uses present stem, strong past the preterite plural stem; weak past retains dental stem. forweorðe/forwurde preserves ð:d alternation; ārīse/ārise differs in root-vowel length while prefix ā stays long. Tense/mood labels remain distinct where sęnde or gelīefde are syncretic.

Present base is present stem+-ende, retaining gemination where appropriate. Strong past base uses the fourth stem+-en, selected forceorfende/forcorfen and weorpende/worpen. Weak gemētende/gemētt and geglęngende/geglęnged follow their lexical weakI stems. Selected worpen is the bare base; optional geworpen is a valid alternative under the source participle-prefix rule.

audit_recommendation_precedence: The reconciled canonical contract assigns scope. Audits provide evidence; complete morphology does not establish every sense or construction.

local_support.title: Opening passive and proportion
local_support.text: Ymbseald means surrounded/beset; mid introduces the surrounding dangers. Efne reinforces the assertion. The paired swā clauses with comparatives mean the greater the worldly dignities, the fiercer the dangers. This proportional construction remains supported, distinct from prior equal-degree swā…swā.
local_support.display_obligation: Print this exact support beside the assigned task or reading and keep it visible during assessment; no unsupported recall is required.

local_support.title: Examples recognized and understood
local_support.text: Be ðǣm is a separate dative prepositional phrase, by/from that: it points back to the preceding proposition as the basis for inference. Bȳsena is the accusative examples governed by the two modal infinitives oncnāwan and ongietan. The paired verbs reinforce one act of understanding; do not treat bȳsena as dative because be appears earlier.
local_support.display_obligation: Print this exact support beside the assigned task or reading and keep it visible during assessment; no unsupported recall is required.

local_support.title: Tree, growth, result and reflexive
local_support.text: The relative ðe identifies the tree. Wiexð is the exact source third singular grows, beside the earlier selected wiext. The result clause ðæt hit hlīfað explains how it grows: so that it towers above the other trees. Brǣt hit means spreads itself; this hit is accusative and refers to the same tree. The first hit in the result clause is its nominative subject.
local_support.display_obligation: Print this exact support beside the assigned task or reading and keep it visible during assessment; no unsupported recall is required.

local_support.title: Storm and passive comparison
local_support.text: Sęmninga is suddenly. Gestęnt is singular present, assails/comes on; Cook’s note identifies storm and the following strong wind as its two subjects. Preserve the singular Old English wording; idiomatic English can use plural strike. The two following ðonne tokens function differently: then in the temporal correlation and than after swīðlicor more violently. Gewǣged and geswęnged are supplied passive bases. Se ōðer wudu means the rest of the forest, as the original note says.
local_support.display_obligation: Print this exact support beside the assigned task or reading and keep it visible during assessment; no unsupported recall is required.

local_support.title: Original157n3: hruron
local_support.text: Cook asks for the indicative preterite plural of hrēosan. Supply hruron (all plural persons); the classII plural uses u with s/r alternation. This is reference-only help, not a new complete productive hrēosan paradigm or an unaided recall task.
local_support.display_obligation: Print this exact support beside the assigned task or reading and keep it visible during assessment; no unsupported recall is required.

local_support.title: Cliffs and coordinated infinitives
local_support.text: Swā bið ēac gelīce be… means it is likewise also with/concerning…. The plural hīe refers to the cliffs/crags. Hlīfiað means tower and feorr ūp far up. Onginnað begin governs both feallan and hrēosan; full strengthens ðearlice, very violently. The two fall verbs can reinforce one collapse rather than name two chronologically separate events. Tō eorðan gives the destination to the earth.
local_support.display_obligation: Print this exact support beside the assigned task or reading and keep it visible during assessment; no unsupported recall is required.

local_support.title: ðā-ðe
local_support.text: Ðā-ðe is the exact joined source spelling of plural relative ðā with ðe, which. It is nominative plural as subject of standað and refers to muntum and dūnum. The prior compound-relative construction is reused with this explicitly supplied spelling; no new headword or unrestricted joining rule is inferred.
local_support.display_obligation: Print this exact support beside the assigned task or reading and keep it visible during assessment; no unsupported recall is required.

local_support.title: Mountains and punishment
local_support.text: Supply the repeated it is likewise with/concerning after Swilce ēac. Hēah is adverbial high with standað. Ðā-hwæðre means nevertheless. The mountains pay the penalty of their pre-eminence: the ðæt-clause explains that penalty. Geneahhe is often, preserving the source’s unmarked spelling beside dictionary genēahhe. Geðrēade, geðrǣste and geslægene are agreeing plural passive participles: punished/battered/struck by heavenly fire and thunderbolts. These exact forms do not assign three full new paradigms.

local_support.title: The human conclusion
local_support.text: The first subject is the high powers; hrēosað and feallað reinforce their fall, and weorðað tō lore means come to destruction. The second subject is the wealth of this world, which becomes sorrow (tō sorge). The third is these earthly wonders, which come to nothing (tō nāhte). The tō-result expressions are supplied; they are not instances of the earlier nominative-predicate become frame.

grading_obligations.target_specification: Keep the two ordinary negatives, plural subjects, prophets as hearing objects, future-context present belief without an added will auxiliary, and the supported indefinite concessive clause. End that concessive clause with present subjunctive ārīse.
grading_obligations.useful_error_diagnosis: The supplied indefinite hwā is not an independently recalled indefinite system. Final-verb control belongs to the concessive clause.
grading_obligations.alternatives_policy: Accept defensible Old English alternatives while separately judging compliance with any explicit original target. Supplied material remains visible; no independent recall is demanded.

assigned_items.prompt: Provide for yourselves (184. a) friends (156. n) in (on) God’s poor (ðearfa). Ye have many Lazaruses (Lazaras) now lying at your gates.

source_locator.prompt: Provide for yourselves (184. a) friends (156. n) in (on) God’s poor (ðearfa). Ye have many Lazaruses (Lazaras) now lying at your gates.
source_locator.origin_category: exact source with declared typographic normalization

assigned_items.editorial_directions: Translate the exact prompt using the supplied helps and the decoded original controls.
assigned_items.target_specification: Use plural command tiliað, dative reflexive ēow under184a, genitive friends under156n and on plus the supplied poor-people location/association frame. Preserve the plural addressees, supplied Lazaras and the supported accusative lying description at their gates.

local_support.title: habbað … licgende
local_support.text: Licgende means lying, accusative masculine plural describing the object Lazaras. In this supported construction habbað has the people as its accusative object and the participle describes their situation at the gates. This does not assign a new general habban-plus-participle system.

local_support.title: on Godes ðearfum
local_support.text: In the exact acquire-friends expression on Godes ðearfum means in/among God’s poor. The group after on is dative plural; Godes is its internal dependent genitive. This local domain use is supplied and does not add a general new sense to every on phrase.

local_support.title: æt his geate; æt ēowrum geatum
local_support.text: Use æt with dative place: æt his geate at his gate, æt ēowrum geatum at your gates. His is the personal genitive possessor; ēowrum agrees with plural geatum. The exact at sense remains locally supplied, even though the form æt is already productive in another frame.

local_support.title: Lazarus
local_support.text: Lazarum — Lazarus, the poor man in the parable; plural Lazaruses denotes people like him (accusative singular with Latin ending, directly attested in the cited Luke16.24 quotation); Lazaras — Lazarus, the poor man in the parable; plural Lazaruses denotes people like him (accusative plural, naturalized -as; exact Cook prompt help)
local_support.scope: Printed exact local aid; no independent recall of the supplied dependency is required.

grading_obligations.target_specification: Use plural command tiliað, dative reflexive ēow under184a, genitive friends under156n and on plus the supplied poor-people location/association frame. Preserve the plural addressees, supplied Lazaras and the supported accusative lying description at their gates.
grading_obligations.useful_error_diagnosis: Do not make friends an ordinary accusative object of tilian, or infer a general habban-plus-participle tense from the supplied lying phrase.
grading_obligations.alternatives_policy: Accept defensible Old English alternatives while separately judging compliance with any explicit original target. Supplied material remains visible; no independent recall is demanded.

source_spans.learner_text: Ǣghwilc hēah ār, hēr on worulde, bið mid frēcnessum ymbseald; efne swā ðā woruldgeðyngða bēoð māran, swā ðā frēcnessa bēoð swīðran. Swā wē magon, be ðǣm, ðā bȳsena oncnāwan and ongietan. Ðæt trēow, ðonne, ðe wiexð on ðǣm wudubearwe, ðæt hit hlīfað ūp ofer eall ðā ōðru trēowu and brǣt hit, ðonne sęmninga storm gestęnt, and se stranga wind, ðonne bið hit swīðlicor gewǣged and geswęnged ðonne se ōðer wudu. Swā bið ēac gelīce be ðǣm hēaclifum and torrum, ðonne hīe hlīfiað feorr ūp ofer ðā ōðre eorðan, hīe ðonne sęmninga feallan onginnað, and full ðearlice hrēosan tō eorðan. Swilce ēac be ðǣm hēagum muntum and dūnum, ðā-ðe hēah standað ofer ealne middangeard, ðā-hwæðre wīte habbað ðæs ealdordōmes, ðæt hīe bēoð geneahhe mid heofonfȳre geðrēade and geðrǣste, and mid līegum geslægene. Swā ðā hēan mihta hēr on worulde hrēosað, and feallað, and tō lore weorðað, and ðisse worulde welan weorðað tō sorge, and ðās eorðlican wundor weorðað tō nāhte.
source_spans.selection_rationale: Complete first argument: opening thesis about danger with high station; connected tree, cliff and mountain examples; explicit return to human power, wealth and earthly wonders. The following paragraph begins a distinct luxury/death argument and is unassigned.
source_spans.unassigned_continuation: Printed158.5 through the end of ReaderVIII; begins Ðēah wē ðisse worulde wlęnca tilien swīðe.

local_support.title: Opening passive and proportion
local_support.text: Ymbseald means surrounded/beset; mid introduces the surrounding dangers. Efne reinforces the assertion. The paired swā clauses with comparatives mean the greater the worldly dignities, the fiercer the dangers. This proportional construction remains supported, distinct from prior equal-degree swā…swā.
local_support.display_obligation: Print this exact support beside the assigned task or reading and keep it visible during assessment; no unsupported recall is required.

local_support.title: Examples recognized and understood
local_support.text: Be ðǣm is a separate dative prepositional phrase, by/from that: it points back to the preceding proposition as the basis for inference. Bȳsena is the accusative examples governed by the two modal infinitives oncnāwan and ongietan. The paired verbs reinforce one act of understanding; do not treat bȳsena as dative because be appears earlier.
local_support.display_obligation: Print this exact support beside the assigned task or reading and keep it visible during assessment; no unsupported recall is required.

local_support.title: Tree, growth, result and reflexive
local_support.text: The relative ðe identifies the tree. Wiexð is the exact source third singular grows, beside the earlier selected wiext. The result clause ðæt hit hlīfað explains how it grows: so that it towers above the other trees. Brǣt hit means spreads itself; this hit is accusative and refers to the same tree. The first hit in the result clause is its nominative subject.
local_support.display_obligation: Print this exact support beside the assigned task or reading and keep it visible during assessment; no unsupported recall is required.

local_support.title: Storm and passive comparison
local_support.text: Sęmninga is suddenly. Gestęnt is singular present, assails/comes on; Cook’s note identifies storm and the following strong wind as its two subjects. Preserve the singular Old English wording; idiomatic English can use plural strike. The two following ðonne tokens function differently: then in the temporal correlation and than after swīðlicor more violently. Gewǣged and geswęnged are supplied passive bases. Se ōðer wudu means the rest of the forest, as the original note says.
local_support.display_obligation: Print this exact support beside the assigned task or reading and keep it visible during assessment; no unsupported recall is required.

local_support.title: Original157n3: hruron
local_support.text: Cook asks for the indicative preterite plural of hrēosan. Supply hruron (all plural persons); the classII plural uses u with s/r alternation. This is reference-only help, not a new complete productive hrēosan paradigm or an unaided recall task.
local_support.display_obligation: Print this exact support beside the assigned task or reading and keep it visible during assessment; no unsupported recall is required.

local_support.title: Cliffs and coordinated infinitives
local_support.text: Swā bið ēac gelīce be… means it is likewise also with/concerning…. The plural hīe refers to the cliffs/crags. Hlīfiað means tower and feorr ūp far up. Onginnað begin governs both feallan and hrēosan; full strengthens ðearlice, very violently. The two fall verbs can reinforce one collapse rather than name two chronologically separate events. Tō eorðan gives the destination to the earth.
local_support.display_obligation: Print this exact support beside the assigned task or reading and keep it visible during assessment; no unsupported recall is required.

local_support.title: ðā-ðe
local_support.text: Ðā-ðe is the exact joined source spelling of plural relative ðā with ðe, which. It is nominative plural as subject of standað and refers to muntum and dūnum. The prior compound-relative construction is reused with this explicitly supplied spelling; no new headword or unrestricted joining rule is inferred.
local_support.display_obligation: Print this exact support beside the assigned task or reading and keep it visible during assessment; no unsupported recall is required.

local_support.title: Mountains and punishment
local_support.text: Supply the repeated it is likewise with/concerning after Swilce ēac. Hēah is adverbial high with standað. Ðā-hwæðre means nevertheless. The mountains pay the penalty of their pre-eminence: the ðæt-clause explains that penalty. Geneahhe is often, preserving the source’s unmarked spelling beside dictionary genēahhe. Geðrēade, geðrǣste and geslægene are agreeing plural passive participles: punished/battered/struck by heavenly fire and thunderbolts. These exact forms do not assign three full new paradigms.
local_support.display_obligation: Print this exact support beside the assigned task or reading and keep it visible during assessment; no unsupported recall is required.

local_support.title: The human conclusion
local_support.text: The first subject is the high powers; hrēosað and feallað reinforce their fall, and weorðað tō lore means come to destruction. The second subject is the wealth of this world, which becomes sorrow (tō sorge). The third is these earthly wonders, which come to nothing (tō nāhte). The tō-result expressions are supplied; they are not instances of the earlier nominative-predicate become frame.

original_notes.original_text: This resembles the use of gin in Chaucer, almost as an auxiliary tense-sign, like do in Mod. Eng., the latter not being thus used in OE. In Chaucer it usually occurs as the preterit gan, e.g. in the Clerk’s Tale, 392: “til the sonne gan descende.” See Lounsbury’s History of the English Language. An interesting parallel is to be found in New Testament Greek, as, for example, Acts 1. 1: “The former treatise I made, O Theophilus, concerning all that Jesus began (ἤρξατο) both to do and to teach.” According to Thayer, however (Greek-English Lexicon of the New Testament), there is in its employment always a sense of beginning, in its proper meaning.

original_notes.original_text:
It would be interesting to know from what literary source these illustrations are ultimately derived. They remind one of Shakespeare (Rich. III., 1. 3. 259–260):—
They that stand high have many blasts to shake them;
And if they fall, they dash themselves to pieces.
Cf. also 3 Hen. VI., 5. 2. 11–15. No doubt many Elizabethan parallels could be found; I have noted in Chapman, Byron’s Conspiracy, Act 3, Scene 1 (p. 232 of Shepherd’s ed.), and Byron’s Tragedy, Act 5, Scene 1 (Ib., p. 272). Perhaps the Elizabethans may have derived them from Seneca; cf. the Chorus in Act 4 of the Hippolytus, vv. 1123–1143; Hercules Furens 201; Œdipus 8–11. Seneca may have caught a suggestion from Sophocles, though the parallel is somewhat remote; see the latter’s Antigone, vv. 712–717, and Horace, C. II. 10.

U03-ADJ-USE.evidence_note: Strong/weak conditions and agreement. Cook says weak sometimes after possessives; this is not a universal possessive→weak rule.

U03-STRONG.evidence_note: Complete strong pattern, short/long stems, æ/a alternation, disyllabic syncope and optional loss of -u, -e stems, h-loss and consonant simplification.

U03-WEAK.evidence_note: Complete weak pattern. Selected ordinary Gpl -ra; -a/-ena are explicitly admitted alternatives. Comparative Gpl contraction is explained, not a license to invent arbitrary assimilation.

U03-COMPARE.evidence_note: Regular, umlaut and irregular degrees; comparative weak, superlative usually weak. Selected representative series below, not blanket mastery of all examples.

U03-ADVERB.evidence_note: Adverb formation and degree; wīd→wīde, swīð→swīðe very, sōð→sōðlice truly. Adverbs modify verbs, adjectives or adverbs.

U03-NUMERAL.evidence_note: Cardinal/ordinal spellings and complete one/two/three rules; ordinals weak except ōðer.

U03-POSSESSIVE.evidence_note: Six agreeing first/second-person possessives; third-person genitives indeclinable. sīn not selected.

U03-DEMONSTRATIVE.evidence_note: Full that/this paradigms. Cook prints short-e ðes, not ðēs; selected double-s variants. Instrumental is reference recognition only.

U03-WRIGHT-USE.evidence_note: Positive/superlative predicate strong; eall and ōðer always strong. Full paradigms confirm agreement; mixed-gender predicate exception remains outside present tasks.

U03-WRIGHT-SYNCOPE.evidence_note: Long-disyllable syncope with retention before consonantal endings; analogical micles/miclum explicitly printed; hāligu and hālgu variants; -erra/-erre may simplify.

U03-WRIGHT-E.evidence_note: Full wilde pattern used by ūre, with its separate fem.Nsg exception in §464.

U03-WRIGHT-GEARU.evidence_note: Complete gearu strong pattern (gearone, gearore, gearora; gearw- before vowel) and weak gearwa/gearwe.

U03-WRIGHT-HEAH.evidence_note: Complete contracted hēah strong pattern and weak hēa, hēan. Selected hēanne/hēarre/hēarra/hēaum; source also gives simpler variants.

U03-WRIGHT-COMPARE.evidence_note: Comparatives weak; irregular series and their variants. Does not individually attest every derived case.

U03-WRIGHT-NUMERAL.evidence_note: Plural ān rare with different distributive sense, not cardinal one with plural count nouns; 4–19 generally uninflected before a noun, with separately conditioned inflection outside this unit.

U03-WRIGHT-POSSESSIVE.evidence_note: uncer/incer/ēower explicitly like hālig; ūre like wilde except F.Nsg ūre. ūrre/ūrra may simplify. Combined with §§429/431 yields transparent pattern-derived cells.

U03-WRIGHT-ADVERB.evidence_note: Exact wel/bet/betst and regular -or/-ost pattern; Cook hook spelling selected for bęt/bętst.

U03-THAN.evidence_note: Attested Beowulf469 comparison Sē wæs betere þonne iċ! provides a nominative standard after than with unexpressed repeated copula. Bounded analogous composition, not a claim that all than-constructions take nominative.
U03-THAN.edition: R. D. Fulk, An Introductory Grammar of Old English (2014), corrected open-access reprint, June 2020.
U03-THAN.source_attribution: Beo 469 in Fulk §35. Retain Fulk’s printed betere in this evidence quotation; it is not the selected masculine comparative model in the course.

U12-ROOT-BT-HABBAN-AGREEMENT.claim: The entry distinguishes uninflected participles from inflected and mixed usage with habban. Bare and agreeing realizations are evidenced alternatives, not an exceptionless mapping from English perfect grammar.

exact_examples.analysis: Plural finite subject Hie contrasts with singular accusative hine/ofslægenne. This is evidence for object-linked participial inflection, not participle agreement with the finite subject.

exact_examples.analysis: The coordinated example combines a bare participle with an inflected accusative-masculine participle referring to the object aldor.

lexical_frames.construction: Intransitive gewęndan return with tō+dative endpoint; no new general transitive turn construction.
Gelīefan on+accusative person means believe in that person; independent absolute believe is separately allowed in27.10. Do not infer this accusative from a physical-motion diagnosis.
Forlǣtan leave an accusative thing to a dative recipient, bounded to leaving peace; prior abandonment sense does not establish this frame.
Forgiefan give an accusative thing to a dative recipient. The assigned meaning is give/grant, not forgive.
Āhrēosan fall upon a goal marked on+accusative; independent intransitive fall remains the dictionary sense.
Throw an accusative entity onto/into an on+accusative goal; the patient passive retains that goal. The bare selected past participle is worpen.
Gebiddan pray with an accusative personal pronoun coreferential with the subject. Preserve Cook26.8’s twice-stated184b control; the pronoun need not be translated as an English object.
Gān with on+accusative marks entry/ascent into or onto the named mountain. This is an explicit extension beyond the earlier dōn placement-on frame and objectless go.
Ætīewan show an accusative thing to a dative recipient. Distinguish this weakI transitive verb from prior weakII ætēowian appear.
Geglęngan adorn an accusative person; passive has the person as subject and may add mid+dative material/clothing. No complete active finite system is assigned.
Liccian lick an accusative entity; in27.4 the dogs lick the wounds.
Giving may leave the thing given unexpressed when the context supplies it; retain the dative recipient in27.4.
Beran carry an accusative person or thing to a destination marked tō+dative. This extends the prior carry object frame without changing the object’s case.
Āhębban lift an accusative entity, with optional separate ūp. The source ūpāhōf compound retains its old supplied identity.
Gemiltsian governs dative person; gemiltsa mē is an imperative, not an accusative object construction.
Onfōn receive takes dative thing received: Cook27.8 gōdum is dative plural goods. Earlier fōn catch+accusative is a different frame.
Ārīsan arise intransitively; of+dative marks source. Use the new subjunctive in the supplied indefinite concessive expression.
Tiliað ēow frēonda: acquire/provide friends in genitive, with dative ēow for yourselves. Cook156n and184a are independent case controls; singular command tila has the same frame.

families.analysis: Gold + hord: the first noun specifies the material/content of the second. Checked whole-word meaning is treasure or hoard of gold. The full goldhord paradigm is separately assigned by the nominal editor.
families.production_boundary: Analyze the printed attested word. Hord is a supplied citation, not an extra complete productive noun.

families.analysis: Heofon + fȳr: heavenly fire, fire from heaven. The final -e in exact heofonfȳre belongs to dative singular inflection, not the lexical compound itself. Here it refers to destructive heavenly fire/lightning.
families.production_boundary: Supply the exact reading form and its case. Do not require an unassigned compound declension.

families.analysis: Hēah + clif appears with the combining form hēa- in hēaclifum, high cliffs. Hēa- limits clif adjectivally; -um is dative plural inflection. The visible hēah/hēa relation is a lexical compound relation, not permission to drop h in arbitrary words.
families.production_boundary: The exact compound and clif citation are supplied; no free coinage or complete new clif system.

families.analysis: The attested learning/study noun leornung uses the leorn- family stem with -ung. It is a separate feminine noun, not an inflected finite form of leornian. The printed infinitive citation is supplied; finite learn use was taught earlier.
families.production_boundary: Analyze the attested pair; do not manufacture a noun from every verb.

families.analysis: Gefēra companion and gefērscipe companionship share gefēr-. Citation -a of the weak noun is not retained before -scipe. The suffix gives an abstract relationship in this checked noun.
families.production_boundary: Only the attested pair is required; no unrestricted -scipe formation.

families.analysis: Rihtwīs righteous + -nes gives rihtwīsnes righteousness, a feminine abstract noun. Adjective and noun retain distinct inflectional systems.
families.production_boundary: Use the actual previously taught forms and senses; do not assume all -nes meanings are mechanically predictable.

families.analysis: Īdel empty/void and īdelnes idleness/indolence belong to one attested family. The learned noun sense is idleness, not automatically physical emptiness. Cook301 lists both lexical meanings.
families.production_boundary: Recognize the family without silently extending the adjective or noun sense.

families.analysis: Heofon heaven + -lic yields attested heofonlic heavenly. This is adjective formation, not the -lice adverb ending.
families.production_boundary: Analyze the attested adjective; its full prior inflection is reused, not a new derivation license.

families.analysis: Cook70 explicitly pairs swīð strong with swīðe very, and sōð true with sōðlice truly. The sense of swīðe is learned as very; -e and -lice identify attested adverb formations. These adverbs do not agree with a noun.
families.production_boundary: Adjective bases stay supplied citations; no new swīð or sōð declension and no full adverb comparison system.

families.analysis: In this attested pair un- marks negation/opposition: righteousness and unrighteousness. The suffixal noun system remains the same.
families.production_boundary: Do not coin un- words freely; check the lexical whole.

families.analysis: Berstan burst and tōberstan break up/go to pieces show the attested asunder sense of tō-. Weorðan become and forweorðan perish demonstrate a lexically learned destructive result, not the English preposition for. Cook lists several meanings for both prefixes.
families.production_boundary: All four citation forms are printed support; their familiar finite systems do not make an unrestricted prefix rule productive.

families.analysis: Gōdwębb is the checked purple-cloth word; wyrtgemang is spice/a mixture of spices. These whole-word meanings are taught from the nominal editor’s lexical evidence. No speculative historical dissection is required.
families.production_boundary: No claim that English component substitution guarantees the whole meaning; exact quantity and whole meanings follow source editor evidence.

families.analysis: Gōdum in Hē onfēng gōdum is dative plural of the lexical noun gōd goods, governed by onfōn. Ðā rihtwīsan in Ic geseah ðā rihtwīsan uses the prior substantival adjective righteous people in accusative plural. Absence of a following noun alone does not decide lexical noun versus adjective.
families.production_boundary: Reuse prior u11-articled-righteous-persons; no general rule that every adjective becomes a noun with a new lexical paradigm.

families.analysis: Ealdor chief + -dōm gives the attested leadership/primacy noun. Here the high mountains’ ealdordōmes is their pre-eminence; genitive -es is inflection, distinct from the derivative -dōm.
families.production_boundary: This contextual sense and exact genitive stay supplied; no new full noun system or political meaning is inferred.
